(3) A person commits an offence if, in purported compliance with any obligation to give
information to which he is subject under or by virtue of regulations made under this
Act, he gives any information which he knows to be false in a material particular or
recklessly gives any information which is so false.

(4) A person commits an offence if, for the purpose of obtaining, whether for himself or
another, the issue or renewal of a licence or other authority under this Act or under
any regulations made under this Act, he—
(a) makes any statement or gives any information which he knows to be false in
a material particular or recklessly gives any information which is so false; or
(b) produces or otherwise makes use of any book, record or other document which
to his knowledge contains any statement or information which he knows to
be false in a material particular.
[F32(5) In this section (and in references in Schedule 4 that refer to this section), any reference
to regulations made under this Act is to be taken as including a reference to provision
made in a temporary class drug order by virtue of section 7A.
